title.narrative: Strengthening GCC capacities to expand access to reliable and accurate information through digital public goods, including open solutions

description.narrative: Access to reliable information, knowledge sharing, and open digital ecosystems are essential foundations for inclusive knowledge societies and sustainable development. Building on UNESCO’s Information for All Programme (IFAP), the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Educational Resources (OER), and UNESCO’s broader work on access to information and digital cooperation, this programme will support GCC countries in strengthening policies, institutional capacities, and partnerships that promote open access, open data, and equitable access to knowledge. The programme will focus on raising awareness of UNESCO’s Information for All Programme and supporting interested Member States in establishing National IFAP Committees as national platforms for dialogue and cooperation on digital inclusion, access to information, multilingualism, information ethics, and digital literacy. It will also support the follow-up implementation of UNESCO’s Recommendation on Open Educational Resources through policy dialogue, knowledge sharing, and capacity-building initiatives. Activities will include high-level policy discussions, regional consultations, advocacy events, technical information sessions, and participation in major regional forums such as ICEGOV 2026 in Riyadh and other relevant digital governance events. The programme will also support the promotion of Universal Acceptance and multilingualism in the digital environment through the dissemination of the UNESCO–ICANN Policy Brief Advancing Universal Acceptance of All Domain Names and Email Addresses for a Multilingual Internet. Activities will aim to raise awareness among policymakers, regulators, technical communities, academia, and digital stakeholders on the importance of ensuring that all domain names and email addresses, regardless of language or script, function equally across digital systems. The programme will further support regional advocacy and awareness-raising initiatives linked to the International Day for Universal Access to Information (IDUAI), reinforcing UNESCO’s commitment to inclusive access to information and digital participation for all. Expected results include strengthened national capacities to promote open knowledge policies, increased awareness of UNESCO’s normative frameworks on access to information and Open Educational Resources, enhanced regional cooperation through the Information for All Programme, and greater engagement of GCC stakeholders in developing inclusive and knowledge-based digital societies.
